title.zh: 跃蛙前导滑翔相机：迎面视角（迭代 3）

evidence: Numerical-uncalibrated simulation plus engineering illustration. Nothing was built, flown or physically tested. Hardware values not tagged LIT/CALC are ASSUMED.

scopeArgument.docs19: docs/19 excludes cameras placed along the route in advance or depending on dedicated perch facilities, even if the user places them; it keeps flying/snow devices carried by the user that accompany them autonomously.
scopeArgument.facts: Carried in the holster before/after each run and on the lift; it places itself only during the run, autonomously, on plain snow (no facility); in flight it stays ≤48 m (hard limit); for 12–13 m/s riders it perches only when the rider stops (perched share of skiing time 3.2 % ensemble mean) and for slow riders up to ~20 % of skiing time.
scopeArgument.reading: In scope as an autonomous accompanying flying camera (audit LF-12 agrees). R06 differs because it is hand-placed and static. Caveat: a glider left behind (soft snow, motor failure, strong headwind give-up) becomes an object the user must recover; this is counted as +1 recovery action.

bom.src: ASSUMED (STM32N6-class); iteration-2 choice, kept as the no-vision variant

userSequence.step: morning: clip holster (14 Wh bank) to the hip belt and the UWB tag to the right wrist
lift ride: holster charges the heated glider cell (heater energy counted)
top: draw (wings spring open), hold ~2 s (wind check: LED green/red), toss down the fall line, push off
run: it leads ahead and films head-on; nothing to do
rest stop: it lands ahead and keeps filming; at the push-off it takes off on its own
end (lift approach): glide up to the perched glider (ensemble p90 11.3 s riding, p90 38.3 m) and stop beside it; it folds itself
pick it up and holster it (gloved, ASSUMED 10 s)
end of day: USB-C charge holster and glider

perRun.opsMaxCases: head9_s12/s13: the 2 s launch estimate saw a lull, the glider could not keep pace and was left behind (+1 recovery)

envelope.wind: downslope component of the estimate ≲4 m/s (feasible progress drops to <0 above ≈4.4 m/s: 1.12 v_stall + tailwind > speed cap) → tail 6 and 9 m/s refused (0 %); headwind to 6 m/s full, 9 m/s 42 % mean with ops 3 in 2/3 (estimate lull); cross 9 m/s 92–96 %; total ≤12.5 m/s, gusts ≤15 m/s
envelope.riderSpeed: avail 64–79 % on the 6-case wind subset for vTarget 7–13; vTarget 14 refused
envelope.snow: groomed only (powder strands it, ice slides 17+ m)
envelope.cannotPassHonestly: Ensemble avail ≥80 % is not reachable with honest physics at 164 g and the 14.9 J line: the tail-6/9 m/s cases (6/39) are physically unfilmable for an 11 m/s-progress rider (floor airspeed + tailwind exceeds the KE speed cap; a hop-and-perch mode yields 2–3 % and leaves the glider >50 m behind). Without them the remaining 33 cases average 88.9 %.

regulation.class: Unmanned aircraft even when gliding. 168.5 g < 250 g, ground speed ≤12.6 m/s < 19 m/s: designed for EU C0 (A1, operator registration because of the camera, never over assemblies). US: recreational sUAS < 250 g, TRUST, CBO rules, VLOS — a lead device in front of the rider is the most plausible VLOS layout.
regulation.vlos: A lead device flies in front of the rider, inside their visual line of sight while they ski, unlike a chase drone behind them. The 50 m follow-me radius (SRC-43) is respected by design (sepMax ≤50 m in nominal).
regulation.resortRules: Many resorts ban drones or require written permission (docs/20). A perched object on the piste edge also falls under resort and FIS-code rules on obstacles. Hi-vis colours, an LED and the take-off-away/landing-postponement logic reduce the risk, but resort approval is needed.
regulation.othersSafety: KE in the ground frame ≤14.1 J by the speed cap (criteria line 14.9 J). Touchdown KE ≤3 J in light wind and up to 5.7 J in a 13 m/s gust. Other skiers are avoided by landing-site selection; a skier hitting a perched 125 g glider is not modelled.
regulation.geofence: 48 m separation hard limit in flight (ensemble max in flight 42.5 m p90); the follow-me derogation applies to flight; a perched glider is not flying.
regulation.resortGate: Written resort permission is a gate (Vail-type bans). Not fixable by design.

exposurePerRun.note: expected other-skier passes per run, rate = density × 10 m/s × 2r × time; densities ASSUMED; detection 80 % ASSUMED for the on-board person detector

othersSafety.note: Poisson estimate with ASSUMED densities: most exposure is the ~74 s of flight 3 m above the piste, not the perch. Medium density ≈2 flight passes within 5 m per run before avoidance. A skier hitting a perched or low-flying glider is not modelled.

honestLimits: Nothing is physically tested: perching flare, skid take-off, claw braking/anchoring, gimbal/EIS performance, pick-up time and the pointing accuracy of UWB angle-of-arrival are ASSUMED.

Forces are point-mass; the attitude model only drives the camera. Sub-span turbulence is absent from the shared wind field, so airframe shake may be under-estimated (sensitivity ×2 shows gimbal+EIS absorb it in the model).
Wind estimate at launch has only ≈2 s of data (shared windEstimate clamps at t=0): lulls let head9 runs launch and get left behind.

Rider-speed sensitivity: flight separation reaches 54 m (vTarget 11) and 50.5 m (vTarget 13) in 1 of 6 cases each; L/D −30 % variant reaches 56 m — the 48 m hard limit is not yet robust outside the nominal rider.
tdKE max 6.9 J > own 5 J line in tail 3 m/s (downwind flare); slide max 7.2 m.
physicalTestsNeeded: set-down skid take-off on groomed/chalky/wind-packed snow at −10 °C incl. cross-slope and into-wind runs (≥20 trials, ≥95 %)
pointing: two-antenna UWB + GNSS + ToF height on the glider vs wrist tag at 15–45 m in motion; elevation error σ ≤0.5 m equivalent is load-bearing (5° elevation error → 44 % subset avail)
wind estimate at launch: holster/glider sensor bias and lull detection in 6–9 m/s headwind (head9 lull → ops 3)
KE protection flight log: 3-D ground speed ≤13.3 m/s with crab/trim/land-now in 3–6 m/s tailwind gusts
lift-geofence landing precision: within 10 m of the pick-up spot, never within 10 m of other people
perching flare/touchdown on snow (≥30 landings), claw anchor, perch hold to 15 m/s gusts
gloved pick-up/holster time (8 s ASSUMED) and set-down time (2.5 s ASSUMED)
22° M12 lens on a GM2-class gimbal: bandwidth/residual

iteration3Summary: Shared judging rules: avail on col.riding (no-fly = 0), jitter = p90 of the shared footageStability over flown cases, simulated standstill (set-down + lead wait + landing wait + simulated glide/side-step to the glider + 8 s pick-up ASSUMED), every wind gate on windEstimate(), headClear judged.

Launch: no hand toss. The rider sets the opened glider on the snow 1.5 m beside the skis; it runs away from the rider on its skid and lifts off (headClear min 1.89 m; the iteration-2 toss gives 0.05 m and fails, scenario launch_toss). The rider pushes off when it leads by 15 m (30 m when the estimate says it cannot out-pace this rider).

Wind gates on the shared estimate: (1) |w̃| ≤ 12.5 m/s; (2) progress gate — the glider can fly a sustained track (≤2.5 m/s drift) downhill at least as fast as this rider (learned progress) with 3-D ground speed ≤ vCapG−0.3 and thrust+slope; (3) in flight: progress check → land ahead and film from the perch, never chase; (4) gust interlock (air-data peak or mean+2.5σ > 15 m/s → hold/land); (5) into-wind approach when a downwind landing would over-speed.

Independent speed protection (A2-LF-02): KE-feasible crab air heading (3-D incl. terrain-following descent), GNSS ground-speed trim and min crab angle, airbrake, altitude hold instead of terrain following when the airbrake saturates, GNSS land-now at KE cap − 0.4 m/s, skid-run abort at the limit, no lift-off outside the follow-me radius. Gate bypassed on all 7 refused cases: KE max 13.43 J, flight separation max 44.0 m.

Pointing (A2-LF-03): sourced fusion — UWB PDoA azimuth σ 5° (Qorvo DW3000 ±5°), GNSS relative position σ 1.5 m/axis (two M10-class receivers, 1.5 m CEP each), elevation from UWB range + own height (ToF) + slope, height error σ 0.5 m. Ensemble pointing RMS 4.7° (vs 1.2° assumed in it. 2). UWB-only azimuth (τ 2 s): subset avail 72.1 vs 74.4 %; 5° in elevation too (audit style): 43.7 % — the height geometry is load-bearing (kill test). Vision variant (shared 11 g / 2.5 W compute, person detection): better pointing but 172 g lowers the KE cap: 69.3 % → not chosen.

Camera: shared 4K 16:9 module (16 g / 2.5 W, A2-LF-06) behind a 22° lens (narrower than 30° because elevation no longer depends on UWB); mass 142.5 g × 1.15 = 163.9 g; KE cap 13.48 m/s; limiter target 12.18 m/s 3-D.

Lift geofence is positional (mapped entry ±4/3 m); it lands on a pick-up spot 5 m past and 4 m beside the entry; retrieval glide simulated. Coarser 4×3 prop (Vp 28 m/s, T0 1.3 N ASSUMED) for headwind lead flight. Shorter dwell trigger (gapGo 14 m) and a lane that widens to keep the rider ≥17 m when the lead is short (crop fits the 22° lens).

modes.lead: normal: lead 20–35 m ahead, head-on footage (97 % of usable footage is from flight)
modes.slowRider: rider progress ≲8 m/s: leapfrog perches (perch share 10–30 %, rider-speed table)
modes.hopAndPerch: when the in-flight estimate says it cannot keep pace: lands ahead, films the approach from the perch, does not chase (follow-me radius); with the gate bypassed this gives only 2–3 % avail and the glider is left behind (+1 op) — so the launch gate refuses these runs instead
modes.fastRider: rider progress > ≈11.9 m/s (vTarget 14): refused by the progress gate (cannot lead under the KE cap)

envelope2D.note: gate: the glider can fly a sustained track (≤2.5 m/s drift across the piste) with downhill progress ≥ the rider's (thrust + slope gravity, 1.12 v_stall floor, ground speed ≤ vCapG − 0.3); downslope wind + = tail

round4.evidence: numerical-uncalibrated simulation on the round-4 shared rules (48 cases, helmetAt, bodyPx, ARTEFACT_PX, no idealised actuators/estimators in judged runs); not physical verification; G-MATURE closed

firstPrinciples.tailwindProblem: Straight downwind lead: ground speed = w + V_air,min must stay under the KE cap √(2·14.9 J/m) (minus 1.0 m/s gate margins, ×1/cos15° for the terrain-following descent). So w_max = (√(29.8/m) − 1.0)·cos15° − 1.12·v_stall. Round 3: m 164 g, v_stall 7.03 → w_max 4.18 m/s. Both levers matter: lower v_stall (area, CLmax) and lower mass (raises the cap and v_stall drops with √m). Crabbing/S-turns do not beat it: the convex hull of feasible ground velocities gives mean progress ≤ (c² − V_a² + w²)/(2w) and the reversals through downwind exceed the cap unless w + V_a fits anyway; reversals through upwind cost ~2.6 s each at ≈w ground progress.
firstPrinciples.massConstraint: Mass cannot rise: the rider's straight-line speed (≈13 m/s on the 15° run) already sits at the KE-capped limiter target (vCapG − 0.6). A first morphing build at 181 g (shared vision board, larger tucked wing) dropped calm avail from 98 to 90 % because the cap fell 0.6 m/s. Mass +10 % sensitivity: subset avail 65.6 vs 94.6.
firstPrinciples.chosen: Feathered span-morphing wing (LisHawk, Ajanic et al. 2020 Sci. Robot. 5:eabc2897: wing 0.117→0.165 m², min speed 7.6→4.0 m/s): tucked 0.55 m / 0.05 m² (fast, headwind, compact, low perch wind load), extended 1.0 m / 0.10 m² CLmax 1.25 (ASSUMED) → v_stall 5.14 m/s, w_max 6.12 m/s (tucked only: 2.77). Mass held at 168.5 g by a smaller tucked panel, a 1.2 Wh cell and the 4 g NPU + 1.5 g preview sensor instead of the 11 g board. Spread feathers double as the air brake (Δcd 0.6) needed because terrain-following in a tailwind is a steep AIR path.
firstPrinciples.tail9: Tail 9 m/s is physically out of reach for any 15° lead glider of this mass: the convex-hull progress bound with the extended wing is 10.5 m/s (< rider ≈10.9) and keeping pace would need v_stall ≤ 4.55 m/s at 168 g. Refused by the gate in all three seeds (honest envelope).

designChanges: feathered span-morphing wing with a rate-limited servo (0.6 s full travel + 0.1 s lag), commanded from the wanted airspeed; spread at the KE cap as an air brake; tucked on the snow
anticipating ground-speed limiter (GNSS acceleration, 1 s look-ahead) for throttle cut and air brake

robust launch gate: evaluated after ≥5 s of shared estimate history (the glider sits on the snow measuring), worst case over a ±1 m/s cross-slope box and +0.4 m/s downslope; gust hold at launch = refusal (picked up again)

crab reversals through downwind only if that passage stays ≥0.5 m/s under the KE cap; give-up/stop landings in a tailwind go cross-wind (no backward drift out of the radius); no lift-off >34 m from a moving rider; separation-limit landings cannot be cancelled by a go-around
follow-me radius pull (lane drawn towards the rider above 30 m), chase-after-pass in non-tail wind, no voluntary mid-ride perches in a tailwind, in-flight model-only perch decision removed

live framing: causal tracker of the measured line of sight — NPU person detection (15 Hz, 80 ms, 3 % box noise + 3 % pose bias, dropouts → UWB/GNSS fallback) with GNSS relative-velocity feed-forward (σ 0.3 m/s, 0.1 s old); EIS residual vs a causal 1 Hz low-pass; causal min-hold zoom
avail/pxMed on bodyPx; headClear half-span envelope 0.275–0.5 m with morph; pitot noise on the gust interlock; air-data wind starts at the bias (no true-wind initialisation)

simulated handling (MODAPTS, glove ×1.3, boot ×1.2, seeded misses): set-down 3.1 s, pick-up/snap 5.2 s mean (p90 5.7); self-folding wings, magnetic snap holster; holster 0.32×0.091×0.086 m incl. walls = 2.50 L

jitterRms.stat: p90 of footageStability subjectRms over flown cases (live tracker crop)

round4.envelope: downslope (tail) wind estimate ≲5.8 m/s after the robust box (true ≈≤5.5–6 m/s); total ≤12.5 m/s, gusts ≤15 m/s; rider downhill progress ≲11–12 m/s (vTarget 14 m/s refused); groomed piste; 9 m/s headwind 62–92 %%. Tail 9 m/s refused (physics).
